title: Sorting and Paging Results
description: Sort your result sets with ORDER BY, deduplicate with DISTINCT, and page through large result sets with OFFSET-FETCH or TOP.

data.text: By default, SQL Server returns rows in an unpredictable order. When you need consistent output — whether for a report, a screen, or just readable results — you use ORDER BY to sort the rows. This lesson also covers removing duplicates and paging through large datasets.

data.title: Basic ascending sort

data.text: By default, ORDER BY sorts in ascending order (ASC). Add DESC for descending:

data.title: Descending sort on one column, ascending on another
Sorting by column position
data.text: You can sort by the column's position in the SELECT list (ORDER BY 2 DESC sorts by the second column). It is shorter, but less readable than naming the column — prefer explicit names in production code.
DISTINCT removes duplicate rows from the result set. It is especially useful when you are joining tables and may produce repeated combinations.

data.title: DISTINCT — one row per city
NULLs and DISTINCT
data.text: DISTINCT treats NULL as a value, so all NULLs collapse into a single row. If you need to count NULLs separately, handle them explicitly with COALESCE.
There are two main ways to limit how many rows a query returns:

data.title: TOP — get the first N rows
data.code:
-- Top 10 most expensive products
SELECT TOP(10) product_name, list_price
FROM   production.products
ORDER BY list_price DESC;

data.title: OFFSET-FETCH — page through results
data.code:
-- Page 2, 10 rows per page (skip the first 10)
SELECT product_name, list_price
FROM   production.products
ORDER BY product_name
OFFSET 10 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY;

rows: OFFSET n ROWS FETCH NEXT m ROWS ONLY
Page through a large sorted result set

data.title: OFFSET-FETCH always needs ORDER BY
data.text: SQL Server will raise an error if you use OFFSET-FETCH without ORDER BY, because paging without a defined sort order is meaningless — the 'next 10 rows' could change between executions.

data.title: What to remember
points: ORDER BY defines the sort — ASC ascending, DESC descending; you can mix per column
DISTINCT removes duplicate rows from the result
TOP(N) is the quick way to get the first N rows
OFFSET-FETCH pages through sorted results but requires ORDER BY
Always pair sorting + limiting for reproducible output
